name: ScanForge File & Theme Security
author: adnan.limdi

sections.description:
ScanForge File & Theme Security helps site administrators and WordPress developers audit installed plugins and themes for unauthorized file modifications, missing official files, and suspicious code patterns.

Key capabilities include:

  • WordPress.org Checksum Verification: Compares local plugin files against official WordPress.org MD5 checksum manifests (with transient caching and automatic cache invalidation on plugin upgrades).
  • Static Signature Auditing: Scans eligible files (.php, .phtml, .ico, .inc) against local JSON threat signatures with exact file and line-number reporting.
  • Batch & Single-Target Scanning: Run a full audit across all loaded plugins and themes or inspect a single plugin or theme directly from the dashboard or Plugins screen.
  • Configurable Scan Thresholds: Adjust the maximum file size limit (in MB) and control whether /vendor/ directories are scanned or skipped.
  • Checksum Cache Management: Purge cached WordPress.org checksum transients on demand from the scanner dashboard.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the scanforge-file-security directory to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin directly through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate ScanForge File & Theme Security through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to Tools → ScanForge Files (or click Launch Scanner on the Plugins list) to configure scan options and run an audit.
sections.faq:
Where do I access the file scanner?

Go to Tools → ScanForge Files in your WordPress admin dashboard, or click ScanForge File Audit next to any plugin on the Plugins page.

Why does a plugin with a `/vendor/` folder report differences during checksum checks?

Some plugins bundle Composer dependencies or build artifacts that differ from or are absent in official WordPress.org checksum manifests. Use the Scanner Configuration panel to adjust how /vendor/ directories and file size limits are handled during audits.

How can I force fresh checksum lookups from WordPress.org?

Click Purge Checksum Cache on the ScanForge File & Theme Security dashboard to clear cached checksum transients before running a new scan.

1.1.0

  • Added configurable /vendor/ directory handling and max file size (MB) limit in Scanner Configuration.
  • Improved WordPress.org plugin and theme repository detection and status reporting.
  • Added checksum transient purging on plugin upgrades and via dashboard action.

1.0.1

  • Initial public release on WordPress.org.
